name: Panta Class 8 Common Repairs Reference - Elite Alignments
source: Elite Alignments - What Are the Most Common Repairs for Class 8 Trucks?
usage_note: Curated retrieval reference based only on the supplied Elite Alignments article. This is practical shop-observation/general maintenance information, not an OEM diagnostic manual. Use it for symptom/category triage and common-repair context; do not infer that a listed component is the cause without diagnosis.

documents.title: Common Class 8 brake system repairs
documents.summary: Elite Alignments identifies brake issues among frequent Class 8 repairs. Listed repairs include slack adjuster replacement, S-cam wear, brake shoe/drum resurfacing or replacement, air-line leaks or freeze-ups, and faulty air dryers allowing moisture buildup. Poor stopping power, squealing and pulling to one side are warning symptoms.

documents.title: Common Class 8 diesel engine repairs
documents.summary: The source says common diesel-engine trouble can involve fuel systems, EGR and oil-pressure problems. Its frequent-repair examples include fuel injectors, turbochargers, oil pumps and cooling repairs involving hoses or water pumps; it also lists glow-plug malfunction. Warning signs mentioned are white smoke, power loss and burning oil. Treat this as source-specific general repair context rather than an engine-model diagnosis.

documents.title: Common Class 8 transmission repairs
documents.summary: Elite Alignments lists clutch adjustment/replacement for manuals, transmission-fluid service or leak repair, ECU reprogramming for automated manuals and torque-converter failures among common transmission work. Sluggish acceleration and gears refusing to engage are cited as warning signs.

documents.title: Common Class 8 suspension and steering wear
documents.summary: The article lists leaf-spring hanger or cracked-spring replacement, airbag/compressor issues, shock replacement, and worn kingpins or tie rods as common suspension/steering repairs. Bouncy ride, vehicle lean and steering play are identified as early warning symptoms.

documents.title: Common Class 8 DPF SCR EGR repairs
documents.summary: The source lists clogged DPF requiring forced regeneration, EGR cooler failure, DEF dosing-pump issues and SCR catalyst degradation as typical aftertreatment problems. Warning lights, poor fuel economy and limp mode are cited symptoms. Diagnosis should still identify the actual DTC and root cause before forcing regeneration or replacing components.

documents.title: Common Class 8 cooling system failures
documents.summary: Elite Alignments lists cracked radiator tanks or hoses, failed fan clutch, plugged radiator fins, faulty water pump and low coolant caused by leaks among common cooling-system problems. A rising temperature gauge is treated as an urgent warning because continued overheating can cause severe engine damage.

documents.title: Common Class 8 electrical and charging repairs
documents.summary: The article lists starter or alternator failure, shorted wiring harnesses, sensor replacement including NOx/DPF examples, and battery/cable corrosion as common electrical repairs. Slow starting, dead batteries and multiple warning lights are cited as signs of electrical trouble.

documents.title: Common Class 8 wheel-end and bearing repairs
documents.summary: The source identifies overheating hubs, grinding/screeching, bearing repacking or replacement and axle-seal leaks as wheel-end concerns. It warns that an untreated bearing failure can damage the spindle and require more extensive hub repair.

documents.title: Class 8 common-repair triage rule
documents.summary: Use this source to rank broad repair categories and recognize symptoms, not as proof of a failed part. For a real truck complaint, combine vehicle make/model/year, engine/transmission, mileage, exact symptoms, active DTCs, operating conditions and inspection/test results before recommending parts or repairs.
